second_order: Building and keeping the shared r/CFB football
theme_note: These codes share the practice of learning the canvas, choosing and drawing the room's football and lettering, recruiting workers, maintaining borders, handing work across shifts, and using scripts to restore the shared mark. They vary from early instruction and design choice to manual repair, defense, and scripted rebuilding.

second_order: Working out borders, truces, and fights with canvas neighbours
theme_note: These codes hold together as participants respond to overlapping designs and neighbouring groups by proposing peace, setting borders, reporting attacks, restraining retaliation, bargaining over shared backgrounds, and relaying help. What varies is whether the neighbour is treated as a partner, rogue threat, invader, or unresolved peace request.

second_order: Making, helping, and fighting over school marks and rivalry jokes
theme_note: These codes share school- and rivalry-facing canvas work: calling for team logos and scoreboards, offering coordinates and templates, placing or repairing pixels, indexing projects, trading help, vandalizing rivals, and disputing scripts. They vary from one-title appeals and sightings to sustained work exchanges and cross-school arguments.

second_order: Finding, judging, and fixing the April food flairs
theme_note: These codes share the practice of making the temporary flair change legible and locally accountable: discovering assignments, asking what hidden images mean, praising or disputing regional fit, proposing replacements, repairing broken flairs, and reconstructing the vanished set. What varies is access trouble, local explanation, moderator response, and later recovery.

second_order: Turning football talk into College Food Board play
theme_note: These codes hold together because participants use food to keep doing familiar r/CFB things: staging fights, ranking rivals, making coach and conference parodies, swapping recipes and restaurant advice, recalling stadium food, and stretching offseason jokes. What varies is mock hostility, practical help, local memory, and collaborative wordplay.

second_order: Posting and spotting April Fools football jokes
theme_note: These codes share making, solving, borrowing, or calling out April Fools football headlines, banner clues, and collaborative joke formats outside the food-flair practice. They vary from one-post hoaxes and parody news to banner detection and edited-question play.

second_order: Turning the finish into a football postgame and mark inventory
theme_note: These codes share retrospective work after placement stops: recognizing the end, mourning and thanking, joking in a postgame register, assigning blame and credit, archiving images, inventorying surviving marks, correcting ownership, and weighing successor canvases. What varies between sportsmanlike closure, continued rivalry, technical confession, and disputed attribution.

second_order: Redirecting event image posts under r/CFB rules
theme_note: These codes share the subreddit operators' practice of removing direct-image event posts under standing posting rules and directing material toward the accepted venue. The removed posts vary from celebrating a B1G corner to demanding retaliation or showing the final seconds.

second_order: Backing the women's team through the r/CFB Twitter account
theme_note: This single code records a distinct community-support practice that belongs with none of the canvas, food-flair, food-play, hoax, moderation, or postgame exchanges.
